reason: Quote under 'Best practices > Account-level separation' says to use account-level separation and keep production certificates in separate accounts from testing and development certificates.
Pricing quote states ACME-enrolled certificates are charged per domain at issuance and each automatic renewal, and are valid for a maximum of 45 days.
Quote states the private key is held by the ACME client and never leaves your systems, and ACME certificates appear in ACM inventory but cannot be bound to AWS integrated services.
ALB certificates page: alternatively create a CSR, get it signed by a CA, then import the certificate into ACM or upload it to IAM.
ALB quota table row: Certificates per Application Load Balancer (excluding default certificates), default 25, adjustable Yes.

Quote supports only 'must specify exactly one certificate, the default certificate'; the clause that more certificates go in a certificate list used with SNI is only in the surrounding context, not in a quote.

Quotes state renewing or replacing does not affect in-flight requests pending routing, new requests use the renewed certificate, and ACM certificates on the load balancer can be renewed automatically.
ALB certificates page quote: ACM supports RSA certificates with 2048, 3072, and 4096-bit key lengths, and all ECDSA certificates.
Quote on public certificate characteristics: ACM certificates are trusted by all major browsers including Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; Java also trusts them.
Quote under AWS Amplify: if you connect a custom domain, the Amplify console issues an ACM certificate to secure it.
Quote under Amazon API Gateway: a custom domain name requires an SSL/TLS certificate, and ACM can generate or import it.

Quote supports daily events from 45 days (private/imported) and 30 days (public); the qualifiers 'default', adjustable and 'changeable with PutAccountConfiguration' come only from the next context sentence, not from a quote.
Quote: if this CAA error appears after the request was validated, you must update your CAA records and request a certificate again.
Quote: after ACM validates the domain it checks for a CAA record; configuring a CAA record is optional.
Two quotes: a CAA record specifies which CAs may issue for a domain or subdomain, and it isn't a substitute for requirements such as validating domain ownership.
Quote states verbatim that Route 53 supports CAA records.
Quote under the Solution (migration) heading: the team can quickly issue new certificates for new domains using ACM.
Quote under the Opportunity heading (prior to the CloudFront migration): to update certificates Trainline had to submit a request to another provider and wait.
Quote: each ACM certificate must include at least one FQDN and can include additional names, including bare domains (www.example.com plus example.com).
Quote: certificates are regional resources; for ELB in more than one Region request or import a certificate per Region; you cannot copy a certificate between Regions.
Document history row dated June 18, 2026 adds ACME; What's New post dated Jul 6, 2026 says the ACME endpoint issues public TLS certificates with a 45 day validity.
Document history row dated June 1, 2026: CT logging opt-out no longer available; all public ACM certificates are automatically recorded in CT logs.
Document history row dated November 8, 2022: added ECDSA support when requesting a public ACM certificate.
